claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in polycrystalline tungsten are governed by interactions between coherent nanoprecipitates and the grain-boundary network.
The grain-boundary network acts as a structural mediator between coherent nanoprecipitates and mechanical behavior.
Interactions between coherent nanoprecipitates and grain boundaries enhance dislocation glide.
Interactions between coherent nanoprecipitates and grain boundaries enhance dislocation absorption.
Enhanced dislocation glide and absorption improve tungsten toughness.
The proposed initial material is polycrystalline tungsten with a grain size of 10 μm.
The proposed initial material contains 0.1% coherent nanoprecipitates.
The intervention introduces coherent nanoprecipitates with sizes of 10–50 nm.
The intervention targets a nanoprecipitate number density of 10^22 m^-3.
The comparison is to be conducted at 1000–1500 K under fusion plasma-facing conditions.
Introducing the nanoprecipitates is predicted to increase high-temperature plastic strain by 30% relative to tungsten without nanoprecipitates.
Introducing the nanoprecipitates is predicted to increase toughness by 25% relative to tungsten without nanoprecipitates.
The proposed baseline is polycrystalline tungsten without nanoprecipitates tested under the same high-temperature conditions.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply only over 1000–1500 K.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply to materials with grain sizes of 5–20 μm.
A less than 10% increase in both high-temperature plastic strain and toughness after nanoprecipitate introduction would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial material is said already to contain 0.1% coherent nanoprecipitates, while the intervention is described as introducing nanoprecipitates and the unperturbed baseline contains none. The pre-intervention state and the intervention arm are therefore not clearly distinguished.
